speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head T of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At last year's MND huddle, Minister Lawrence spoke about the importance of partnership.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Last year also marked the 60th anniversary of the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We can all see how much our living environment has changed through the decades of careful planning by MND and its agencies.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In 2019, the MND has similarly achieved much.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Home buyers can now plan better, project sites are now half year ahead of schedule.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For vulnerable families, more options and support from the new Home Ownership Support Team.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Looking ahead, the MND has not just focused on immediate issues but, like it has always been, visioning far head.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: There is excitement over the future of our city and our home.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Draft Master Plan 2019 offers a glimpse.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can the Minister provide some details on the new projects to be funded?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Minister share why there was a drop in the mean CONQUAS, and how MND and BCA intend to promote better quality workmanship?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In line with that, can we better promote more local talents in the construction industry?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I, and perhaps many Members of this House, have seen fewer cases of residents appealing for flats.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Those who do usually have more complex circumstances.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is therefore a reflection of how our housing policy has improved.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But there are still some who need more help or better options.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What more can MND do to help home-seekers access their flats quicker?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With the open booking of flats, it has afforded Singaporeans who want quicker options to select and book their flats.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Last year, MND organised an intense round of outreach across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of these roadshows were led by Minister Lawrence Wong himself.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This was to raise awareness on the LBS.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I would first like to ask what has been the sign-up rate for 2019, and if the roadshows have helped to increased understanding and also encouraged more to take it up.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Another group that I have spoken about every year has been support for vulnerable families and individuals.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am heartened by the work of the Home Ownership Support Team that Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling announced last year.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can the Ministry perhaps share how many have benefited from the targeted help so that they can achieve home ownership?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For singles, the challenge remains that there are many waiting in line.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Supply of 2-room flats for singles are still lagging behind demand.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Does the Ministry intend to expand on the supply this year?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For unwed parents and divorcees with children, which my colleague Mr Louis Ng has championed for passionately over the years, can the Ministry also share how it intends to better support them?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For elderly Singaporeans who wish to age in place, some have also indicated that they prefer additional services such as "assisted-living" facilities.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned last year that MND and MOH are in discussion on this.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can the Minister therefore share if there has been progress made and if there are now firmer plans for the Government to undertake such assisted-living projects?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We all know that we are constrained by our physical size in Singapore, but our circumstances have driven us to find innovative and forward-looking solutions to afford us the best use of this limited resource, so that we can maintain a careful balance of responsible and responsive land usage.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Amidst a rapidly changing global environment, what are we doing to retain our competitive edge while ensuring that our city remains liveable for our people, even with the changing aspirations?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our city centre is perhaps our most recognisable and visible skyline.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, it is also the hardest to rejuvenate.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the progress made to date?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I further urge that we continue to ensure that the Central Business District (CBD) and our city centres are not exclusive enclaves, but accessible and open to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Another topic that I have been passionate about is how our redevelopment and rejuvenation cannot be at the cost of our heritage.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of our buildings have been lost over the years in the name of progress and better land use.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I applaud the Ministry's efforts in recent years to better protect our built heritage.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I return to the Minister's emphasis on partnerships.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As we work with professionals and stakeholders to build the future Singapore, our towns, our workplaces, I would like to urge for more community involvement in the plans, so that the very people who live, work and play in these areas have a stake in shaping it.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For estate upgrading, we have seen a successful example in Tampines Central.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How will the Ministry better encourage such efforts?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Lively Places Programme, which was a pilot by HDB last year, has seen enthusiastic response.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What projects have come out of this initiative?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I would like ask the Ministry to expand on this programme throughout all our towns in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: On a related effort, we are known as a City in a Garden, a vision first expoused by our chief gardener, the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Over the last 50 years, we have made much progress in greening Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have become a Garden City and then A City in a Garden.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What are the Ministry's plans for the next bound of he greening of Singapore?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How can Singaporeans also be more involved in this effort?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of our multi-storey car park roof decks, for example, are often empty.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I therefore urge that NParks will consider a more ambitious programme to green those roofs and promote more community projects.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Related to this, of course, is our national efforts to combat climate change.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I welcome the announcement of the Green Towns Programme.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our new flats and commercial buildings should also be designed to take full advantage of natural air flows so as to reduce the need for reliance on air-conditioning.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In further light of COVID-19 and the slowing economy, many developers that I have spoken to have found it difficult in the last few months.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: There have been manpower shortages due to slow return of workers, there have been issues with supply chain and equipment, and all-round uncertainty over the economy.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Chairman, we are not done building Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Municipal issues concern all residents, and so each resident should have a stake in the shared living environment and be able to contribute their unique viewpoints and experiences to shape it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: At the same time, the diversity of residents' perspectives and needs should be taken into account.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Could the Municipal Services Office (MSO) share how it is enabling residents, at the individual level and as a community, to have a say in municipal issues?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Chairman, since its inception, HDB has played a critical role in ensuring affordable and accessible housing for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is an institution at the forefront of public housing.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: No other Government agency in the world can boast that it has provided for over 80% of its people the selection of quality public housing it had, served by comprehensive networks of amenities.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: HDB flats are the de facto homes for our newly-weds and many of them will progress to upgrade to bigger units.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: MND launched the open booking of flats last year.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is understandable that HDB has been calibrating the size of flats based on a combination of the size of the family unit and affordability.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This has generally resulted in smaller flats being constructed.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have observed at recent Edusave Merit Bursary Awards ceremonies in my constituency that there seems to be more families with more children, that is, three or more.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These families usually have a domestic helper or live with grandparents, so extra rooms and more living space are needed.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, greening and renewing our housing estates is an important initiative to increase our green cover and promote environmental sustainability.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I note that community roof gardening and installation of solar panels are also some of the initiatives that the newer housing estates benefit from.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, we must not neglect the older, mature housing estates.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Despite the regular upgrading and maintenance projects, the difference between the older and newer estates can be quite stark due to the availability of community amenities, deployment of technology, amongst others.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Safety of the building structure and living areas of the mature estates and flats are very important to ensure that those living in them are safe and sound environmentally, particularly, our elderly Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope the Minister will also explore the usage of solar panels in all the roofs of mature HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As rejuvenating all estates would be a massive project, may I suggest assessing the gaps between the infrastructures in comparison to the newer ones, and prioritising estates with a wider disparity?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: HOST can do regular checks of HDB units by block to see if there is a common flat-wide issue that can be rectified before it worsens and affects other residents' safety.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Chairman, recently I took a drive back to where I grew up in from when I was a baby until I was about 12 years old.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: We used to call it "Hougang luck kor jiok" in Teochew, which roughly translates to "Hougang six pieces of stone".

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Basically, when I mentioned that to the elderly folks, there is a certain warmth in that.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Because of that, I realised that there are places where I had gone to when I was in Secondary school, such as Farrer Park where we used to play football, which are still being preserved.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Strangely, the place I went back to, which is "Hougang luck gor jiok", where I grew up in, the rental unit above a provision shop is still there.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: It is just that one stretch of provision shops and some of the shops are still there – very old – but everywhere else has changed.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: So, that preservation was really meaningful to someone like me.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: I think, for every town, heritage is the identity and soul of the place.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: Would the Ministry consider having that as part of its policy when doing town planning for all the major towns to have a certain heritage to exist for a longer time period?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: We have become a Garden City and, now, A City in a Garden and, in the near future, City in Nature.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Today, greenery is all around us, with parks and gardens close to our homes and workplace, trees along our roads and vertical greenery on some of our buildings.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: But as we develop, there will always be increasing trade-offs between greenery and other infrastructure developments.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Can we continue to grow as a city while remaining green and liveable?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: At a time when our challenges are becoming more complex, partnering Singaporeans across multiple domains to tap on our diverse strengths is vital and our citizens also have a greater desire to contribute, to be heard and to act.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Government has done an excellent job of engaging communities in building Singapore.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, the public was involved in the Draft Master Plan 2019 process through workshops and exhibitions.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The community is also increasingly involved in directly shaping and caring for the areas around them, such as residents managing their community gardens via the Community in Bloom programme.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: As we make plans to rejuvenate our city and enter into the next phase of our greening journey, we must get the community involved at an early stage.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: These engagements will help to foster a greater sense of communal bonding, for the public will also feel a stronger sense of ownership in the space that they have helped to build and, thus, there is a higher chance of better utilisation of these rejuvenated spaces, as they are the outcomes of the community's involvement.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Chairman, this cut is on ensuring that our public housing is affordable and accessible.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I note that MND increased the household income ceiling for subsidised flats last year.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: My questions are supply-related and are as follows.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Two specific questions: One, will there be a dedicated section in HDB’s website to address housing queries from single unwed parents?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, the website merely states that single unwed parents are eligible and asks these applicants to directly contact HDB.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Such developments will bring in new amenities like rooftop gardens, exercise equipment, playgrounds, eldercare and childcare facilities and eateries to complement the old-world charm of mom-and-pop shops, open void decks and good old-fashioned coffeeshops.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Hougang has welcomed two BTO projects over the years and we will be looking forward to welcoming another one this year.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I wish to highlight some design integration issues of such new projects in the hope that future developments will take into consideration these feedback and concerns.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: First, I wish to highlight that the void decks of new BTO blocks are no longer functional.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Residents living in these new blocks can get lost walking in their own void decks.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The number of pillars and walls have literally transformed the new void decks into a maze, forcing residents to use the service road in the estate.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: This is certainly a safety concern for residents who need to cut across the precinct to get to their destination daily.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Furthermore, due to the maze-like design, void decks, chairs and tables have become hidden in secluded corners in these new BTO blocks.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Most of the time, these amenities would end up being misused by noisy drinkers, chain-smokers and rowdy teenagers to hang out in the wee hours of the night, away from prying eyes.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Noise and second-hand smoke will ensue and residents will end up suffering as a result.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Next, I wish to highlight that more could be done to better connect the new precincts to the older part of the estate.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: In the two new BTO precincts in Hougang, the Town Council had to build extra ramps, footpaths and stairs, in addition to the few designated access points, in order to facilitate the safe movement of residents on the ground.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Although it is human nature to take shortcuts, the planner should look into providing a more barrier-free integration of the new precinct to the surrounding built-up of areas at the design stage.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: This will benefit residents on mobility aids or with baby prams, as it is really not easy to navigate the maze-like void deck of new BTO blocks just to use the designated access point.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It may be a challenge for HDB to design better void deck spaces for now but it is certainly doable to have a truly barrier-free integration of new and old precincts in a mature estate for a start.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh, you can do your three cuts.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, recent Built-To-Order (BTO) sales launches had attracted many flat applicants.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But for successful applicants, in fact, the three to four years' waiting time is not short.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To facilitate better planning for both individual households and HDB, would the Ministry consider allowing HDB to share information at the beginning of each year about the planned BTOs to be launched in the next one to two years?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: HDB could also allow applicants to register their interest in advance.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, the demand and supply information could be made available in real time, enabling applicants to make informed decisions earlier.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: All these data will also enable HDB to plan ahead to meet demand.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If financial assistance is given to first-time buyers, whether they are families or singles, to buy resale flats is quite generous.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Yet, some of these buyers cite various challenges finding a suitable resale flat in mature estates.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The reasons include both financial and non-financial ones.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry share which are the top five obstacles these first-time buyers encounter and what further assistance, such as grants, can be provided to them?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Lease Buyback Scheme provides a monetisation option for our elderly while allowing them to continue staying in their homes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is, indeed, 两全其美, a solution which offers the best of both worlds.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many households have actually applied for LBS to date?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, how many households per room type are under the scheme?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Among these flat owners, how many have to use the proceeds from the lease sale to fully discharge their outstanding mortgage loans?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some seniors are worried about outliving their remaining lease.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Lastly, how will the Ministry increase awareness of the scheme among our seniors?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I seek to enquire under what circumstances the HDB will pay in full for such repairs.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In my ward of Eunos in Aljunied GRC, there have been repeat episodes of failing block facades in a specific group of blocks at Jalan Tenaga.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Professional Engineer appointed by the Town Council whose report is available to the Ministry has suggested that the underlying cause of the failing façade is down to shortcomings during the construction phase of the blocks.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: These blocks were constructed less than 30 years ago.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: As the façade of similar blocks in the precinct have failed in an identical or almost identical manner over the last few years, should not the HDB, as building owner, undertake to fully cover and reimburse the costs of the façade damage, repair and pre-emptive investigation of other similarly constructed blocks?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Arasu Duraisamy, you can do both your cuts.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: The Minister also shared about efforts to raise public awareness of the scheme.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: Can the Minister share how has the take-up rate been since the extension of the Lease Buyback Scheme to the larger flats and what are some of the efforts to raise public awareness of this Lease Buyback Scheme?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: The Minister also mentioned that MND and MOH would conduct focus group discussions to seek views on the proposed concept for assisted living in public housing and that Assisted Living Typology flats would be launched in Bukit Batok in 2020.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: Such assisted living flats would be smaller, but they would have more communal and shared spaces for residents to interact with one another.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: Can the Minister share the findings from the focus group discussions that MND and MOH conducted?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: Can the Minister also share the kind of features these assisted living flats will have and when will they be launched, the number of units that will be made available and who will be eligible to buy these flats?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: Over the years, MND has made changes to its housing policies to support diverse housing needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: With these policies, the Ministry has continued to make efforts to better support single unwed parents who are in genuine need of housing.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: These include enhancements to frontline communications and the willingness to review every request made by unwed parents, among others.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: However, some may need more space, especially when their children are growing older.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: Can the Ministry consider reviewing access to bigger HDB flats for unwed parents to better meet their housing needs?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: MND has, over the years, increased attention to support rental households towards homeownership.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: This support has contributed to the steady increase in these households becoming homeowners.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
text: Can MND provide an update on the progress of these initiatives?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Our perception of families has long revolved around the nuclear family unit comprising two parents and children.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We should take a lighter touch on personal matters, such as marriage and life decisions, when making policy.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The "case-by-case" approach allows us to use discretion but there is a lot of uncertainty for this group.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Yes, we want to encourage marriages to remain strong and reduce reliance on state resources.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But can we shift our paradigms and include single unwed parents in the composition of what a "family nucleus" is.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Last year, I met Gina (not her real name) who is a divorcee.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She originally had sole care and control of her son but it was eventually changed to shared care and control.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She has successfully applied for an HDB flat when she had sole care and control but it was later rejected at the key collection stage as the care and control was changed to a shared one.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was unable to obtain mutual consent from her ex-husband even though he was already staying in a private property and did not need an HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been years since the divorce and, due to various other circumstances, she is still renting a place to stay in.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Her ex-husband continues to stay in the private property.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon, you can take both your cuts.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Chairman, to promote the take-up of Electric Vehicles (EVs), I would like to ask the Minster whether he will consider opening up the carparks that are maintained by URA and HDB to more than one operator so that they may install EV chargers and whether such EV chargers can be opened up to the general public for their use, instead of only restricting it to the operators' own EVs.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many residents have asked me if they can park their normal conventional cars in the EV lots and they have asked me why BlueSG gets to park in the prime lots right in front of their flats.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether he can consider or he can educate us on how he intends to will allocate prime real estate between supporting EVs and the needs of residents who might have elderly folks or young children.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have appealed for Lift Upgrading Programme (LUP) for these blocks for many years and I have raised this issue in Parliament since 2012.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The profile of these blocks: the residents are greying, there are many elderly residents, some of them are wheelchair bound, many have mobility issues.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To them, having a lift is an existential need, it is not a good to have.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They become very vexatious when they see that public money is being spent on a nice garden as part of the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) but not the lift that they have been asking for many years as part of the LUP.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: HDB has cited the need for financial prudence in order to maintain cost effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But I feel that financial prudence should be about not overspending above a projected cost, a certain limit.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It cannot be, but HDB has been telling me this and it is not about putting an arbitrary limit on the costs without taking into account our residents' well-being.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I hope there can be a resolution to this issue soon, that the Minister can help my residents at Block 115 and 119 of Marsiling Rise to get lifts.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I hope that more than a 150 blocks in the rest of Singapore, the residents will get lifts soon, because I believe that that we need to ensure that everyone gets high quality living regardless of when his flat was built or where his flat was built.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Some of us in this House had asked for periodic updates about the fate of the remaining blocks without LUP.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I have also asked HDB to look into segregating these blocks into two categories: those with technical constraints and those with cost considerations.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I urge the Ministry to share these numbers.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: These residents have been caught in between the wait for good news or to move out for the longest time.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: And any housing agent would tell you that it would be tough to offload a flat without direct lift access unless the owner is prepared to take a hit on the market valuation or selling price.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I have asked in this House for HDB to let these residents decide if they are willing to pay a little more for direct lift access since funding per flat has to be fair and equitable.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Let these residents decide on the share of the marginal cost.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh, you can do both your cuts.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: I just want to find out, since then, has HDB been able to find new solutions to implement LUP for at least some of these blocks or install some interim devices which can help to transfer residents with mobility issues from their floor to the next floor which has lift access?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: The residents told me they like to age in place and they prefer to stay there.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: I would also like to ask how many households in need of direct lift access due to medical or mobility reasons had approached HDB for housing assistance to date?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: How many of them have been able to move to suitable flats with the assistance of HDB?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: How many families have actually bought their flats with HST's assistance to date?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Due to the numerous hardships experienced by these families, would the Ministry consider providing additional grants or more flexible mortgage payment conditions for them?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: In addition, can HDB provide further assistance to encourage them to become homeowners by accepting the HDB rentals they have paid cumulatively as the downpayment for their own HDB flat subsequently?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Last year, I had called on the Government to consider a change in its policies to allow some elderly singles to rent a flat alone on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If we do not make adjustment to our policies, where do these elderly singles go?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Should we force them to stay with a co-tenant that they do not know?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If we do, the risk is that they may quarrel frequently over minor issues.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Or they may end up with health issues if either of the tenant suffers from some illness.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There are some seniors who are estranged from their families.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They approach me at Meet-the-People Session and say they desperately need a rental flat.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When I ask them why are they not staying with their families; the bitterness in the relationship shows in their face.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I have also met seniors who had married a foreign spouse.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They cannot rent a flat with a foreign spouse.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Then, what do we do for people like them?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I accept HDB's intention of not wanting seniors to live by themselves so that they can help look after one another.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I think in a "CNA Insider" documentary, there was a story about a senior, 65 years old, who died alone.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, this current policy may have led to some sleeping on the streets or void decks.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The situation is untenable and I would urge HDB that we should do more to help these vulnerable seniors.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I ask HDB to consider reviewing this policy.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: But conflict between co-tenants is a problem more than reported.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: It is difficult for complete strangers compelled to stay together.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many live miserably with frequent quarrels and even fights.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The Community Mediation does not work for them for many reasons.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: These affect the well-being of many co-tenants, also cause depression in some and others resorting to become rough sleepers.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Does MND screen potential tenants to be free from mental illnesses or medical conditions before putting them together?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: If not, can there be such assessments for all potential tenants put in place?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Can HDB offer more partitioned rental flats under JSS to provide more privacy?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Can HDB provide newer models of HDB rental flats with better use of space and cost as well as giving privacy to tenants?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Those that seek rental flats are usually the disadvantaged and more vulnerable members of our society that our Government can assist with more of their housing needs.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I want to urge our Government to review JSS, which had been in existent for the last 30 years.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Singapore has progressed in the last 30 years and it is time for Singapore to be more gracious towards the most disadvantaged group in our society, in providing them the basic need of roofs over their heads.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: It is time to tweak this policy for humane reasons.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Will MND allow flexibility for rental flats tenants to opt for single tenancy, especially for those with no family members to share with, while also giving tenants the flexibility to share with co-tenants for companionship and mutual support if they so choose.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: There are many needy families with children living in HDB rental flats.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of them have lived in rental housing for more than six years and some more than 10 years.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: What are the schemes in place and the success rate of such schemes, to assist them in looking for better options in their housing needs and to help them get out of their predicaments?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: These standards do not apply to the Public Rental Scheme.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This results in families of five or six squeezing into a 1-bedroom flat, or even families of more than 10 in 2-bedroom flats.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Research demonstrates that overcrowding has a deep and adverse impact on both adults and children.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: There are significant associations between the number of persons per room and an index of psychological health.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Family ties erode: the parent's authority over the child diminishes as they are unable to accommodate the child's needs; adult family members prefer to stay outside their home till late; conflict occurs more frequently in the home; children do not have enough space to play, rest and study, which directly impacts their academic performance and overall development.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In light of the above, I have three questions specifically for the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How is the act of placing children in 1- or 2-room HDB flats with three to 10 other people in line with Singapore's obligation to primarily consider the best interests of the child under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Chairman, we sometimes wonder why we do not frequently come across people with disabilities and special needs in our community.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: They surely exist even if they are not the majority in our population.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I would imagine like everyone else, they too need a place to live, learn, relax, move about freely and socialise.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I believe this may be the wish of some them, but they do face challenges of not being able to do so in a carefree manner.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: People with disabilities and special needs often require the care of a guardian who can assist with their daily needs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is natural for their family members to be protective to reduce the likelihood of them being mistreated by strangers who are not aware of their special needs' conditions.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: To minimise awkward situations, people with special needs are often confined to their home, school or places where they can be fully accompanied.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Second, mental barriers and confidence in own abilities.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With lesser exposure to the broader community, there are fewer opportunities for people with special needs to experience and understand how to manage social interactions or overcome some living issues.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This has an impact on their self-confidence and their willingness to break the silence in seeking help.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Third, the existing public amenities in the process of being modified to accommodate people with special needs are largely not fully equipped as it was not designed with them in mind at the early stage.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Earlier in the Budget debate, I have raised the need to rally society to be inclusive from young.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But, beside the soft aspects, I would like to ask MND what efforts are taken in our living environment to enable people with disabilities and special needs to socialise and engage in the community.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I suggest the following: One, intentional efforts to adapt designs in our common spaces like the neighbourhood playground, the gardens, to enable their outreach in the community and with designated relief areas for people with special needs to have their private moments.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Two, to create the digital apps with information on venues and services that are friendly to people with special needs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Three, to collaborate or create travel journey tools that shows real live routes which are barrier-free access, wheelchair accessible and leads to reachable areas that are not dead ends.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Familiarity with surroundings and having the right aids in place amongst their living compound are of utmost importance for them.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I hope we can look into using design and technology to ease their burden on the long run.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For example within their home, there can be adjustable household fixtures that are designed to accommodate different physical conditions, hoist to facilitate movements in the toilet and bedroom, voice activated or push controls to automate management of the living environment, sensors within the home that are linked to service care centres or family members and robotic enabled devices that can aid daily activities.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Many people with special needs have hopes and goals in life just like any of us.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Some of these can be achieved through thoughtful designs aided by technology.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We can certainly help to close the gaps in their development journey and enable them to scale new heights, live more independently and fit with greater ease at our shared public spaces.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many contractors told me that they feel discriminated against in recent field contract awards.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The lowest tenderer is an established homegrown contractor.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have about 140 A1 local contractors who have all built up very strong capabilities.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If we do not even support our own contractors, who else will support them?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can we consistently apply the policy of "Buy Singapore First"?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Contractors also shared that they always face payment delays, and hence cause cash flow problems.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some of the causes are: (a) Variation Orders (VO) – the valuation and certification of VOs can drag on for years before they are finally settled; (b) Liquidated Damages (LD) – contractors are imposed LD even before claims for Extension of Time (EOT) and VOs are assessed; and (c) Under-certified payment – it could be due to our "kiasuism" culture, so, the work done on site is often under certified.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: While it is commendable that the Government has taken a long-term view to reducing Singapore's reliance on foreign labour, it should place more emphasis on the quotas of those sectors that Singaporeans would like to work in, which are certainly not in construction or shipyard.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: With emphasis on Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) and Prefabricated Prefinished Volumetric Construction (PPVC), we need more S Pass workers than ever before, as they are more skillful.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Another problem is that Singapore is no longer attractive to some foreign skilled carpenters and tilers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps BCA can help to investigate the reasons and implement measures to solve this issue.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, are they finding it too tedious or too expensive to sit for the Core Trade Skills test?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: With the current push for DFMA and PPVC, are these tests still relevant?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As the COVID-19 situation continues to evolve, the construction industry is facing the full impact of labour shortage, material delays, threat of site lock down and so on, delaying progress of projects.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Government do more to help the construction industry?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, waive the workers' levy during this difficult period.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We also believe that some of the Government policies can be re-examined.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The current crisis could be an opportune time to review and tweak the ABSD regime to make it more equitable and effective as the current regime is not calibrated, to some extent, it is a one size fits all.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is not a call for an easing of the cooling measure but an appeal for a temporary relief for the real estate industry to cope with the current situation.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The following two changes could be considered: first, a re-instatement of the Practical Completion Period (PCP) to six years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Contractors need more time to complete the projects; and secondly, an extension of the five-year ABSD deadline to say six years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Alternatively, the ABSD penalty to be pro-rated based on the number of unsold units, similar to the QC principle.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In anticipation of the high likelihood in project delays, BCA is urging developers not to penalise contractors.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How is this possible if developers are bounded by the five-year ABSD remission deadline which is very punitive?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, the sale of residential units has slowed down sharply, almost to a stop.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope MND can understand the challenges faced by property and construction industry and lend a helping hand.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Let us show solidarity and Singapore together spirit.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I understand that the Act will soon be amended to expand the types of projects that require BCA approval, to include major alteration or replacement works to fixed installations.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In assessing whether or not to approve such works, the BCA will examine the certifications and other paperwork of qualified persons (QPs) engaged by the project owners.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To what extent does BCA itself verify the soundness of these certifications?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The incident of the PIE Viaduct Collapse in 2017 is illustrative.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To date, various professionals associated with the project have been charged and convicted in court.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The QP admitted to having engineers with inappropriate experience, failing to check design assumptions and being aware of errors in calculations by the engineers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: An accredited checker for the viaduct admitted that he had failed to check the designs or perform calculations for the corbels.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In a Parliamentary answer in July 2018, MND elaborated on its standard procedures when dealing with building projects.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Ministry stated that at the plan submission stage, the BCA performs a sampling check of the plans and design calculations of selected key structural elements, to ascertain that the QP and the Accredited Checker had carried out the design and checks in accordance with building control legislative requirements.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: MND further stated that at the construction stage, BCA would conduct targeted inspections on structural works.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Is there a need for agencies to play a larger role in regulating building projects to ensure public safety?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: In the construction sector, there was a focus on offsite prefabrication to improve productivity.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: Many of our local PMETs typically take on supervisory roles of the foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: Now, if they have no more foreign workers to supervise, will they still have a job?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: Thirdly, I would like to ask the Minister if there are new job opportunities for PMETs in the construction sector.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: With growth areas such as Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA) and Integrated Digital Delivery (IDD), are there more programmes for PMETs who can transit into these jobs?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh: Chairman, our construction sector has difficulty employing Singaporeans to fill many of its jobs, from the most humble manual work to PMET positions.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: The main challenges are the unattractive salaries, long work hours and difficult work conditions.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: However, the current COVID-19 outbreak teaches us the importance of having a good pool of local expertise for self-sufficiency.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: It is very important that we maintain a critical size of local capabilities for all job scopes at all levels.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: We should not be too reliant on PRs and foreigners.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, the Built Environment cluster, comprising industries such as the Security, Construction, Environmental Services, Real Estate and Smart Facilities Management, is one of the newest growth sectors.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With the significantly increased demand in related services, particularly smart facilities, environment and security in recent years, it is a sector burgeoning with opportunities and is a potential exportable service we can provide to the world.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How is the Ministry creating good jobs in this cluster and supporting locals to take up these jobs?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Singapore companies across the build environment value chain also collaborate on a complete solution for international infrastructure projects.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What skill sets would be needed for this sector and how can we encourage greater interest for mid-career switches to this sector?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Young PAP and climate activists have proposed that the scheme be reviewed and updated with a more weight given to reducing energy consumption and shifting dependence to greener sources.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The School of Design and Environment Block Four (SDE 4) at NUS is a good example.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It uses a hybrid cooling system that combines the use of air-conditioning and ceiling fans to provide thermal comfort to building occupants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: YP and climate activists have proposed that such features be propagated to new buildings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I understand that there already is a Green Mark for Zero Energy buildings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But we should also raise standards for the other Green Mark schemes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Buildings should be held to a higher standard before we can call them "green".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am glad that NParks have now a 10% increase in height limit for local mixed breed dogs to be re-home under Project ADORE.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The weight of the dog will also be removed as a criterion.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: There is about 20% more local mixed breed dogs can be re-homed at HDB flats each year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can MND provide the rationale for not removing the height criterion as well?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Many more dogs can finally find a forever home if we remove the height criterion.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I understand that MND's concern is that the smaller dogs are generally considered to be more easily carried and controlled, especially in confined spaces such as lifts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: However, size is not a good proxy of the behaviour or temperament of a dog.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Researchers have found that larger dogs are perceived as more obedient, less anxious and less aggressive compared to smaller dogs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: As the saying goes, "It's not the size of the dog in the fight, it's the size of the fight in the dog." As part of the pilot, will MND consider removing the height criterion so that more dogs can be re-homed?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Lastly, it does not make sense that someone who lives in a condo is allowed to keep a pet cat while someone who lives in a HDB flat is not allowed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: HDB has stated that "  are generally difficult to contain within the flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: When allowed to roam indiscriminately, they tend to shed fur and defecate or urinate in public areas, and also make caterwauling sounds, which can inconvenience your neighbours." Surely, these concerns apply to people staying in condos as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Some condo units are even smaller than HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It also does not make sense that one is allowed to keep a dog, and now a big dog, but not a cat, not even a little kitten.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Dogs can also shed fur and defecate or urinate in public areas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We can ensure that pet cats do not roam indiscriminately and are sterilised.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I have seen firsthand how all these simple measures can be taken and people can keep cats in their flats without affecting their neighbours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So many people are already keeping cats in their flats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I find this line of reasoning inconsistent, as this is applicable to all pets and pet owners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But the ban is only specifically on cats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Domestic cats are unlikely to cause the dis-amenities that Minister cited.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Studies have shown that cats spend 25% of their waking hours cleaning themselves; their natural instinct is to cover up and hide their waste, which can be done in a litter box.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Sterilised cats are unlikely to caterwaul and even if they do, some of the reasons could be to alert their owners to outside activity, or they may be in pain or feeling stressed, which are similar reasons why dogs bark too.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Today, many younger families and families of all ethnic groups are pet cat owners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Regulating pet cat ownership in HDB flats will be more beneficial than a ban as it may give many stray cats a loving home and allow cat lovers to take care of their cats at home with peace of mind.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Regulation can include ensuring domestic cats remain indoors, microchipped and sterilised and a framework to encourage community acceptance and having mediation channels for disputes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I read with interest the latest news that the dog size limits for HDB have been relaxed so as to allow more local mixed-breed dogs to be rehomed in HDB flats under Project ADORE.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I hope cats, no less adorable to many Singaporeans, may be included.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, I would like to draw attention to the pet birds trade in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Back in November 2017, I filed a parliamentary question to ask the MND about the frequency that AVA reviews the reference list of birds available for sale as pets to ensure that species which are becoming endangered or threatened are not sold here.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: CITES amends its list once every three years and covers species for which it is illegal to trade.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, in adopting the CITES list, we are saying we will not do anything which is illegal.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Frankly, Chairman, I believe that this is too low a benchmark for us to adopt.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, CITES covers high profile larger animal for which extinction is possible.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many tropical bird species, such as the white-rumped shama, which are threatened and may not be on the CITES list but are included in the IUCN Red List.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The CITES list is also not as comprehensive when compared to the IUCN Red List especially in covering smaller species such as tropical birds.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, the tropical pet bird trade is a multi-million dollar trade which threatens native species.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The situation is so bad that in many forests in nearby countries, some song birds are already extinct.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On the same topic, I would also like to propose an increase in the amount of fines for the illegal smuggling and trade of pet birds.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Assuming a "street value" of $500 per bird, the total value of birds from this smuggling attempt was more than $400,000.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The fine only forms 2.5% of the total value, which is hardly a deterrence for smugglers.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, I really hope that Singapore can show leadership in the conservation of native species and not do what is just the minimum.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The right place for a bird is on a tree branch and not a cage Hopefully, when our grandchildren walk through a forest, there will still be birds chirping and it would not be a silent forest.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I have tried it a few times and found it easy to use and more importantly, effective.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Behind the convenience at my fingertip, I am sure there is a lot of work done behind the scene to make sure the right agency receives the feedback and takes necessary action in time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On behalf of the public, I thank the good men and women at MSO.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some municipal issues are complex and require various agencies to work hand-in-hand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In Tampines, we do have many cases relating to community cats that have been difficult to resolve.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These could be cats roaming at corridors, defecating, scratching cars, caterwauling, irresponsible cat feeding and so on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some residents are bothered by what the cats do, some are just afraid of cats, while others just do not like them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On the other hand, there are many cat lovers who spend their own money to buy cat food and go around the estate feeding them every night.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To many residents, they just turn to the Town Council to solve such issues on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Town Council has to work with HDB which regulates that cats are not allowed to be kept within flats, and NEA, which can go after cat feeders who leave the cat food as litter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, the current practice has also been to work with the Cat Welfare Society (CWS) as a first call.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I have met some staff and volunteers at CWS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They are all very passionate and dedicated people who love and care for cats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They have deep knowledge of how cats behave.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At our last meeting, they recommended sonic repellents to help deter cats from venturing into certain areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, CWS has very thin resources and are not able to follow up fully on all cases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They also do not have authority over cat lovers, cat feeders or pet owners, some of whom may not be very cooperative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, in some cases, CWS has admitted that they would not be able to do anything.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For such issues, could the MSO play the role to coordinate and help set up a sustainable working system to handle such cases?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: Chairman, the work of MSO as part of the Smart Nation Movement has tangibly improved the lives of many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: And many drivers given the feedback that they appreciate the refunds being to them if they end their parking sessions early.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: One such project was the use of drones by the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) for the early detection of maintenance issues, and also a trial deployment of compactor litter bins by NEA for more efficient waste collection.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: I would also like to ask the Minister whether she can consider the use of smart locks that can be remotely controlled.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: These could be used in our shared common spaces like badminton courts and basketball courts.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: While some residents enjoy the use of these facilities, I have also got many residents who will complain to me because of the dis-amenities late into the night.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Chairman, as our country battles the COVID-19 outbreak, I would first start by conveying our appreciation towards all cleaners and workers in municipal services for working hard to keep COVID-19 at bay.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Municipal issues concern all of us as residents and, as Mr Baey Yam Keng said, can be complex and involve multiple parties to resolve.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have made good progress coordinating across Government agencies, Town Councils and other non-government stakeholders, to offer residents services that are prompt, practical and personal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To address complex issues, MSO first clarifies the roles of stakeholders involved.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MSO then works with stakeholders to develop collaborations that tap on their respective areas of expertise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NParks is the first point-of-contact for the public for animal-related feedback.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are tightening the collaboration to manage this and monitoring to ensure that case resolution times and outcomes improve.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Addressing residents' concerns about complex issues often goes beyond coordination, so we emphasise services that carry greater personal engagement.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I recall a case where residents at Pending Road were troubled by unpleasant smells from a nearby flat.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: HDB found the flat severely hoarded and infested with pests.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: HDB worked with Holland-Bukit Panjang Town Council, MSF, PA, IMH, Thye Hua Kwan and Covenant Evangelical Free Church to address the case holistically.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They worked over weekends to clean the flat, obtained financial aid for repairs and provided emotional and counselling support – all to afford long-term self-care to the flat owner and a sustainable solution to other residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is the empathy and resident-centric service we champion.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We aim to raise this to 70% by end-2020.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MSO will go further, beyond coordinating, to forge meaningful connections with, and among residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon asked about MSO's progress in harnessing technology to deliver service improvements to residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The projects undertaken by SLA and NEA under the Municipal Services Productivity Fund are progressing well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2019, we awarded funding for HDB and PUB to trial a smart lock system that Mr Ong has asked, that automates access to maintenance areas in HDB estates, such as rooftops.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will explore the potential for this system to be adapted to other spaces, together with other solutions, such as encouraging residents to be more considerate, as Mr Ong has requested, to address the root cause of community noise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are making other technological improvements to better connect residents to services that meet their needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: First, we are integrating services from agencies and Town Councils into the OneService app, to develop the "Book Facilities" feature for residents to have a single, simple touchpoint to find and book community spaces, such as function rooms, barbecue pits and sports facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In addition, we will introduce new reporting categories, such as "smoking" and "high-rise littering", for residents to highlight specific concerns for investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Second, we are improving accessibility to services, by bringing our mainstay reporting function to where residents are.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With OneService Lite, which involves QR codes posted at places where residents frequent, such as HDB lift landings, users can easily report a case by scanning the QR codes in just two taps, without having to pre-install the OneService app.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Soon, residents can also submit cases via popular social messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram, guided by an AI-powered chatbot.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Third, we are constantly innovating to kick-start future-ready solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Since January, we have been trialling Municipal 360.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Routine feedback submitted through the OneService app will be routed directly to agencies' contractors for speedier resolution.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Residents will be updated with photographs of work done directly by the municipal worker.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Last November, MSO hosted the OneService-Industry eXchange for public and private organisations to share ideas and co-develop solutions for municipal operations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With more collaboration and experimentation, residents can look forward to smarter, more customised service improvements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Even as we expand technological connectivity, we want to connect residents with each other to co-create a better living environment for all.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We agree with Mr Amrin's suggestion to consider the diverse views of residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Certainly, as part of SG Together, we will enable each and every one to have a say and exercise collective choices that will impact their living environment.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For a start, we have included new OneService app features to activate our community to make the changes they want to see.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Residents will be able to poll on local improvement works through "What Say You?" surveys and use the "Community Challenge" feature to take bite-size, meaningful actions that help address issues that concern them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We must also augment hardware with "heartware", by nurturing more community participation and partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We welcome residents to come on board in a variety of ways – as individuals, to inject their unique perspectives, and as a community, to build consensus amid diverse views.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through these projects, we will develop resources that other community groups can use when launching future ground-up initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To sum up, there are many good ideas, diverse talents and new solution possibilities across the community, industry and agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We want to harness these to achieve our common goal of improving our living environment, the SG Together way.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, I will focus on these two aspects today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, we will extend our nature park network.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, we have more than 350 hectares of nature parks, which act as complementary habitats and buffers to our nature reserves to protect them from the impact of urbanisation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is important as the nature reserves are the richest sources of our natural capital.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They contain our primary and secondary rainforests and core habitats for our native biodiversity and wildlife.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is two-and-a-half times the size of the Singapore Botanic Gardens.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Singaporeans can look forward to more places, such as the Rifle Range Nature Park for nature-based recreation, such as hiking and bird watching in future.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Khatib Bongsu is a rich mangrove and mudflat habitat on the north-eastern coast of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Next, we will intensify nature and the greenery in our gardens and parks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, we will incorporate natural designs and plantings in our new and redeveloped parks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: You can expect to see a greater variety of vegetation that resembles the look and feel of natural forests and also benefit from the positive effects of nature on your health and well-being.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, we will naturalise more waterways and water bodies in our gardens and parks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have done this in Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park and Lakeside Garden, where we transformed concrete canals into natural rivers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will incorporate such designs in all our coastal and riverine parks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This will also help to protect against sea-level rise and flooding.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Lastly, we will conserve important native plants and animal species.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of our world's most unique biodiversity call our tropical island home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Singaporeans would have encountered rare native species, such as the Singapore Kopsia, on the left, and tiger orchid, on the right, and this is because of our restoration efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We aim to nearly double the skyrise greenery footprint in our buildings and infrastructure to 200 hectares by 2030.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will focus on greening our industrial estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are amongst some of the hottest areas on the island – hottest in terms of temperature.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the next 10 years, we will plant 100,000 more trees in industrial estates, such as the Tuas Industrial Estate and Seletar Aerospace Park.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These efforts will cool the environment, improve air quality and beautify the surroundings in those industrial estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Lastly, we will strengthen the connectivity between our green spaces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is not enough to intensify greenery in isolated pockets.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we will plant native trees and plants in a multi-tiered structure and create green corridors along roads called Nature Ways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These can be further integrated with pedestrian and cycling paths to form lush and natural park connectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With these, all households will be within a 10-minute walk from a park and, over the long term, where feasible, we aim to make every road a Nature Way.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: During a recent dialogue with friends from the nature community, they shared that the work of greening Singapore cannot be done by MND alone and they are quite right.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
