text: The transformation of Singapore into a City in Nature – a qualitative change – requires close collaboration with other agencies and we will infuse this into our planning and development systems.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But Government efforts alone will not be sufficient.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Various Members also asked how Singaporeans can be more involved in the greening of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want a whole new generation of Singaporeans to carry on this responsibility to keep planting and nurturing trees for the benefit of future Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew sowed the seeds of Singapore's greening movement with the planting of a Mempat Tree in 1963 at a time when the Government was also grappling with serious challenges of unemployment, public health, illiteracy and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But greening, to our pioneers, was serious business back then, and it remains a key priority of national development right till today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A few years ago, I organised a Nature Way planting in Jurong West.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I was standing next to an elderly lady, who was there with her grandson, and they were participating with neighbours and friends in planting the Nature Way.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: After they had shovelled soil around their sapling, I could not help but overhear this elderly lady asking someone to help her take a photograph of her and her grandson next to the sapling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She told her grandson in Mandarin, "Boy, let us take a photo.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Next time, when Ah Ma is gone, come and visit the tree with your family.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It will surely be a lot taller by then.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: You can remember me by that tree." This story stuck deep in me about how our greenery can bind Singaporeans and families in Singapore together, and how one generation takes it upon itself to plant trees for the next generation to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Literally planting trees for the next generation but also figuratively taking responsibility for the long term, not just for ourselves, but for the future.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want this DNA to run deep in our future generations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we will continue this legacy with a new movement – the One Million Trees movement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will do so along our roads, in our parks, estates and green areas, and along some of our coastal areas, we will plant mangrove trees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We may lose some streetscape greenery due to developmental needs, but we will plant back what is lost and more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I recently met with a number of partners, who are passionate about greening, to discuss how this One Million Trees movement can galvanise the length and breadth of Singapore, and bring on-board a broad spectrum of Singapore, especially the next generation, to have a stake in greening Singapore, to have a stake in making sure this place remains liveable, not just for themselves but for the next generation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will involve schools, communities, corporate organisations and many more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes companies on Jurong Island, Keppel Corporation, the National University of Singapore, OCBC, Shimizu Corporation, United Parcel Service (UPS) and many other community groups, organisations and individuals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I am encouraged to see that everyone is doing their part to keep Singapore green.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also want Singaporeans to be more actively involved in the design, development and programming of our parks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes signage design or promoting park etiquette, and partnering our gardeners to do landscape planting.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is one thing for a park to be built near you; it is another for a park to be built near you in which you have had a hand in designing, conceptualising, building and literally knocking the nails into some of the furniture for the park and planting the trees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It also gives a sense of ownership, custodianship and stewardship of the green spaces around you.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also step up efforts to build awareness amongst Singaporeans so that we can live harmoniously with nature.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We invite you to join in our efforts, forge closer bonds with fellow Singaporeans and strengthen our sense of ownership of our environment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Various Members asked about on-going efforts to rejuvenate our CBD and the city and progress of MND's work over the year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We aspire to be amongst the leading cities in the world, where people want to live, work and visit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have introduced the CBD Incentive Scheme for this purpose.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A successful CBD must have a good mix of office spaces, a lively street life, with diverse offerings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To encourage the development of different neighbourhoods in the CBD, we introduced incentives for the conversion of older office buildings into residences and hotels.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Interest and take-up have been encouraging and URA planners are working with interested building owners on this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also introduced the Strategic Development Incentive Scheme to encourage commercial building owners to partner neighbours to comprehensively redevelop a few plots, where transformation is not limited to one building but a whole area along the street or precinct for the public to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: URA is in dialogue with several building owners who are keen with potential to rejuvenate different parts of our city.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But a leading city is nothing without its people and its soul – not just about buildings and shops, but one that reflects the Singaporean attitude of innovation, openness, daring and verve.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng spoke about the spirit of partnership at the launch of the Singapore Together movement last year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At MND we embrace it and will do more to partner Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members have asked how we intend to do so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have private sector partners from 10 precincts all across Singapore on the pilot Business Improvement District programme (BID).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The pilot BID programmes are making good progress.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These stakeholders seek to take a people-centred approach in creating spaces that will draw people into them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, we saw The Lawn next to The Sail and Marina Bay Financial Centre being activated for the first time during the Marina Bay Singapore Countdown, and so expect many more such new initiatives in the coming year and months.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Community feedback was key throughout the Draft Master Plan 2019 process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is another example of how Singaporeans get involved in rejuvenating our city.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We exhibited the plan in March 2019 after rounds of consultation, and gazetted it eight months later.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We assessed each public feedback thoroughly, and incorporated ideas and suggestions where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I am confident that the plan has been made better because of our collective efforts and because Singaporeans cared and participated.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members asked about heritage and conservation of buildings to maintain the character of a city.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Apart from partnerships, we also have to thank many of our colleagues and officers who work assiduously behind the scenes to make this a reality.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, the aborists, conservationists, botanists, scientists in NParks and Gardens by the Bay who dream of a yet more green Singapore and the city planners and innovators who think of ways to energise community partnerships in order to make our city that much more vibrant and exciting.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We look forward to continued partnership with Members of this House as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, may I show some slides at appropriate junctures, please?

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As we continue to remake our city, we must ensure that our firms and our workers in the Built Environment sector keep pace with technological advancements, improve their capabilities and seize upcoming opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 2017, we developed the Construction Industry Transformation Map or ITM, with the industry, the unions, and IHLs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have made good progress in our three ITM transformation areas, namely, Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA), Integrated Digital Delivery (IDD) and Green Buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: DfMA allows us to move on-site construction work into a more controlled working environment off-site, to prefabricate building components for on-site assembly.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This way, construction becomes faster, cleaner, quieter, and of higher quality.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, Teambuild, a local builder, achieved close to 37% site productivity gains for its Valley Spring @Yishun, a HDB BTO project by adopting Prefabricated Pre-finished Volumetric Construction (PPVC).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Here, you can see a module being lifted, to be assembled just like Lego blocks, with the furnishings already fitted inside.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Now, this is an ambitious target but I think that we can achieve this by working together with the industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We aim to make DfMA our default way of building.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon asked how our construction productivity compares with other countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Site productivity data is not available for all countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, our site productivity has improved by over 17% in the last decade, which is significant.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To boost DfMA adoption, we enhanced our Buildability Framework last year, raising standards for larger residential developments and allowing outcome-based solutions to encourage building designs that can be constructed more productively.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will further enhance the framework this year, by progressively requiring higher buildability standards for other development types, including commercial and institutional buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also re-structure the framework to encourage the industry to incorporate DfMA technology into the structural, architectural and Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing designs for buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The public sector will also continue to generate lead demand for DfMA.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The digitalisation of the construction process will facilitate wider deployment of DfMA technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Building Information Modelling, or BIM technology, will allow our architects and engineers to design and build in a virtual setting first.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This improves the accuracy of construction plans and reduces abortive works downstream.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Now IDD takes this further, by leveraging technology to facilitate better collaboration amongst project parties across the building life-cycle, to coordinate production and supply chains, to build more efficiently, to improve building quality and to optimise operations and maintenance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, Guan Ho, a home-grown construction firm, has been using digital technology to track building components as they are fabricated, delivered and installed at Punggol Town Hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This has reduced time spent on project management by up to 30%.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want more local firms to use IDD to build smarter and more efficiently.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SMEs will be guided to assess their level of digital readiness, and identify digital solutions that can benefit businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, site management platforms to plan and monitor construction activities, and facilities management software for operations and maintenance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SMEs can receive up to 70% funding for pre-approved solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SMEs can also use the Digital Roadmap on Training to identify digitalisation courses for employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our industry transformation efforts are not limited to improving productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister emphasised during the Budget, we must remake our city to meet the challenges of climate change.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Buildings account for over 20% of our emissions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Green buildings are hence an important part of Singapore’s climate change mitigation strategy.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are on track to meet our target of 80% by 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also launched the Super Low Energy buildings programme in 2018, which goes beyond Green Mark Platinum standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To share an example – Keppel Land and BCA are working together to transform the Keppel Bay Tower into a Super Low Energy building.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The building uses innovative technologies, including a high-efficiency air distribution system and autonomous lighting control, to reduce energy consumption by about 20%.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is a good example of how existing buildings can achieve Super Low Energy standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the next few months, BCA will co-create the Singapore Green Building Masterplan 2020 with our stakeholders, as we push the boundaries for Green Buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, to push for more energy efficient buildings, we intend to raise the minimum energy performance standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will lower emissions, and also benefit building owners over the building life-cycle.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Concurrently, we will review our Green Mark certification standards, as highlighted by Mr Louis Ng.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: BCA will engage stakeholders to develop shared aspirations for sustainability standards in the Built Environment, and we need to work out how to get there in partnership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Next, we want to enable greater transparency in building energy performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will share more details by this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We call on stakeholders to co-create the Singapore Green Building Masterplan 2020 with us over the next few months.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond improving firms’ capabilities, transforming the construction sector is also about creating more opportunities for our people, as Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Ong Teng Koon mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The adoption of new technologies and digitalisation has created new, higher-skilled jobs in better working environments in the construction sector, and generally they will command higher salaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, with DfMA, we will need more production managers, quality assurance personnel, and logistics and supply chain planners at automated production facilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Tech-savvy local PMETs can also take on exciting jobs such as digital delivery specialists along with the others in the IDD value chain that I mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our sector should be anchored by a skilled and competent local workforce and our firms must also do their part.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The share of local PMETs in construction has fallen over the past decade, even though our total local PMET population has increased.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To help firms build up a strong local core, we are strengthening measures to ensure an adequate pipeline of skilled local PMETs for the industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: BCA and IHLs continually update the curricula of Built Environment courses to meet the industry's evolving needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: BCA also co-sponsors scholarship and sponsorship programmes with the industry to attract students to pursue relevant courses in our IHLs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also progressively introduce new Professional Conversion Programmes or PCPs, to prepare mid-career entrants to join the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, a PMET from manufacturing could be re-skilled as a production manager in a DfMA facility.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Hence, we will develop PCPs for prefabrication job roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Teambuild is developing a firm-level PCP, which will be open for applications later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I have also heard feedback about the shortage of BIM modellers, but firms have not been keen to take in mid-career converts before they are trained.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under the current BIM PCP, participants are trained in BIM while concurrently undergoing on-the-job-training with their firms.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But some firms prefer BIM modellers who can contribute immediately upon hiring.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To address this, we will allow participants to complete their full-time training first, before continuing with on-the-job training with their firms.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, on a full-time basis; they could be ready within three months instead of six or 12 months if they were doing it part-time.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We hope that more firms will take up the enhanced BIM PCP, which will start later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's and Mr Ong Teng Koon's points on the S Pass sub-DRC cuts, our transformation efforts have created attractive jobs for locals.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The S Pass tightening helps level the playing field, and will allow more Polytechnic and ITE graduates to access these jobs, including supervisory roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our local PMETs will still be able to take on supervisory roles, so long as they are open to re-skilling themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As we push ahead with our transformation efforts, we aim to create more of these attractive jobs that I shared earlier, for our local PMETs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I encourage firms to take advantage of our good pipeline of infrastructure projects in the years ahead and attract more local PMETs to join our sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Kimly has also groomed three mid-career BIM modellers under the BIM PCP since 2018.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Kimly paced out the on-the-job-training for these employees to smoothen their transition into the firm, and they are now keen to pick up even more advanced BIM skills, such as 4D/5D BIM simulation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also developed a Skills Framework (SFw) for the Built Environment sector, to map out skillsets required at various levels for key job roles in the construction and facilities management sectors, and their career progression pathways.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More details will be announced later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about ensuring the safety of building works.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For any development, the Qualified Person or QP has a duty to ensure that building and structural plans comply with the building control regulations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In addition, all major building works must be independently reviewed by an Accredited Checker or AC to ensure that the key structural elements are adequately designed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While the responsibility of ensuring structural safety rests with the QP and AC, BCA conducts sampling checks for each plan submission.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Where BCA finds non-compliance with legislative requirements, BCA will take enforcement action.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Penalties could include a fine, or imprisonment, or both.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: BCA regularly reviews the Building Control regime to ensure that it is sufficiently robust.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together with the Institution of Engineers Singapore or IES, and the Association of Consulting Engineers Singapore or ACES, BCA has issued two circulars in 2019 to provide QPs and ACs with guidelines and good practices for plan submissions and supervision.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will help QPs and ACs to improve the quality of their design calculations and ensure that all key structural elements of the project are identified, as well as improve the quality of the QPs' supervision.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, measures have been in place since then and we hope that this will improve the safety record of builders, moving forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Er Dr Lee also spoke about supporting local contractors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore cannot discriminate against foreign firms, in line with our WTO obligations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Indeed, we have been helping local firms to build capabilities as well as strengthen their competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One way we have done so is by parcelling large Government projects, such as MRT lines, into smaller contracts, so that our local firms are able to take up projects while the Government mitigates its risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In recent years, I am also pleased to see more local firms winning large infrastructure projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Er Dr Lee also spoke about payment delays due to Variation Orders, or VOs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: BCA and MOF have encouraged GPEs to process VOs progressively and expeditiously, to ensure timely payments to contractors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We empathise with the current situation and will certainly help where needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, agencies can process VOs based on indicative scope and costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the same time, contractors should include the necessary documentation to support speedy processing of claims.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More recently, we have revised the Security of Payment Act or SOPA, which aims to also help claims for private sector projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If Er Dr Lee can share more details with us, including the treatment of Liquidated Damages (LDs) and progress payments, BCA will look into these specific cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: BCA has advised government agencies to take a sympathetic view when considering Extension of Time or EOT requests, for project delays due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also sought REDAS' support for private sector developers to do likewise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If delays are prolonged, we will consider whether additional measures are necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To ease cashflow concerns from delays due to COVID-19, main contractors can also submit progress payment claims fortnightly instead of monthly, for public sector projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, we are trying to help firms with their cashflow too.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, we have also provided some flexibility in some of our projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some firms with more PRC workers may also face manpower pressure in the short term due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These firms may consider hiring workers from other firms with excess foreign manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Firms can search for eligible workers for transfer via the Foreign Construction Workers Directory System or FCWDS, online.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Built Environment firms can also tap on the support packages announced by Deputy Prime Minister earlier, such as the SME Working Capital Loan under the Enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme, and the Jobs Support Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Er Dr Lee also suggested measures to help developers and contractors cope with COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On foreign worker levies, the Minister for Manpower already said during the Budget debate last week that we are waiving levies for employers with eligible foreign workers serving quarantine leave of absence or stay home notices.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, we have not done so for all foreign workers in general.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As much as we want to help the sector or businesses deal with the short-term fall-out, this should not negate longer term efforts for companies to restructure and become less reliant on foreign manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Levy waivers would run counter to these objectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Er Dr Lee and Mr Alex Yam also asked about the Project Completion Period and the ABSD remission timelines.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government is monitoring the construction industry and the property market closely.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will adjust our policies as necessary to ensure a stable and sustainable property market.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to monitor the situation and see how it goes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to begin by thanking all Members who have spoken up about animal health and welfare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Kindly allow me to share how we will continue to work closely with the community on these issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, one of our key strategies is to reduce the stray animal population and re-home as many as possible, where they will have shelter, food, and adequate care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Launched in partnership with 11 Animal Welfare Groups (AWGs), it involves catching and sterilising stray dogs, or Singapore Specials, as we call them, to sustainably and humanely manage their population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will then rehome as many of the sterilised dogs as possible, while the remaining dogs will be released at suitable locations to live out their lives naturally.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Eight years ago, we worked with our AWG partners to launch Project ADORE to do this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Given the good progress, NParks has recently reviewed the size limits for Project ADORE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: NParks will work closely with our AWG partners to successfully implement the latest revision first before we review the project again.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It bears mentioning that Project ADORE has been successful largely because of careful, sensitive and gradual implementation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: NParks has to balance the objective of rehoming more dogs with the concerns that some residents have over larger dogs in HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is the result of the hard work by our AWGs and NParks officers in terms of outreach on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The second thrust of our work is on increased education and outreach efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: NParks, in collaboration with our AWGs and pet businesses, launched the Pets’ Day Out series in August 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It has provided NParks more opportunities to reach out to and educate pet owners or those interested to own pets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to identify other suitable platforms, such as community events, to reach out to diverse audience groups and garner stronger support from the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, NParks embarked on a review to raise standards in the pet sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As part of the review, NParks has engaged key stakeholders and the wider public through focus group discussions as well as an online survey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There was general consensus that more needs to be done to raise the standards of pet breeders and boarders to safeguard the health and welfare of the animals involved.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Based on the feedback received, NParks intends to take a balanced, risk-based approach to regulating these businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, only commercial breeders and boarders on farmland are licensed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For a start, NParks will focus on improving practices at existing commercial breeding facilities on farmland as the breeding sector deals with young and pregnant animals that require specialised care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will be done by strengthening the licence conditions in areas such as housing and management, healthcare, and traceability of the animals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Concurrently, NParks will step up its enforcement efforts against those who operate a commercial breeding facility without a licence, outside of farmland.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: NParks also intends to license commercial pet boarding facilities based on the scale of their operations, which will depend on factors such as the number of animals handled and the frequency of transactions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Those who help board animals for family and friends, or do it infrequently, will not be subject to licensing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Regardless, all pet service providers, including pet boarders and breeders, have a duty of care towards the animals they handle and they should abide by the Code of Animal Welfare for the Pet Industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond the Code of Animal Welfare, NParks can take enforcement action against pet service providers under the Animals and Birds Act for failing in this duty of care, or for animal cruelty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: NParks will work through the revised regulatory framework with stakeholders and share more details later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing spoke about using the IUCN Red List to regulate the pet bird trade.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is because we regulate wildlife trade according to the requirements of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which uses IUCN conservation status as one of the criteria for categorising species.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: NParks' public consultations on the pet sector review also surfaced the need to enhance the traceability of animals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A robust animal traceability system is critical in protecting public and animal health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the event a pet is diagnosed with an infectious disease, especially one which can be transmitted to humans, such as rabies, it is important to be able to trace its whereabouts and health status.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Pet licensing is one of the measures that enables NParks to do so quickly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope that this will encourage more owners to sterilise and license their pet dogs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For existing owners with three-year licences for sterilised dogs, you will be happy to hear that your licences will automatically be changed to a one-time licence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As part of its pet sector review, NParks is also looking into measures to enhance cat traceability to protect public health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also looking into raising the standards of the veterinary industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our veterinarians play an important role in providing animals with high standards of care and ensuring animal health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They also play a critical role in safeguarding public health as they can help detect the outbreak of diseases that may be transmitted to humans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: NParks will begin engaging key stakeholders on this issue in April this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These are just some of the areas that we have been working on in a relatively short span of time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And there are many other areas that the community has raised, which we are continuing to study and finding ways to balance the needs of the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, the issue of cat ownership in HDB flats, which Assoc Prof Daniel Goh and Mr Louis Ng have raised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that there are residents who are cat lovers and who would like to keep cats in their flats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are continuing to have conversations around how to best strike a balance between residents who are pet lovers, those who are not and those who are concerned about disamenities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB will work with NParks to take a holistic and balanced approach in reviewing and updating its pet ownership policies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last year, I shared about our plans to improve the natural lighting and ventilation in older rental blocks, by removing some flats on each floor to create more openings along the corridors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This year, HDB will commence the improvement works at Chai Chee and Telok Blangah.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At these four blocks, all tenants who are living in the units identified for removal can relocate within the same block, if they prefer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB and local social organisations are closely supporting their transition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB will study where else they can implement similar improvements in future, considering feedback from residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Dr Lily Neo asked about reviewing the Joint Singles Scheme (JSS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Most JSS tenants are prepared to share a flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More than 90% of flat-sharing tenants surveyed did not experience conflicts or difficulties living with their flatmate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nevertheless, HDB will facilitate requests from tenants who wish to transfer to another flat with a different flatmate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For those with extenuating circumstances or medical grounds, HDB is also prepared to consider their requests to rent alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Further, HDB has also been installing partitions in 1-room rental flats for JSS tenants, to provide more privacy for each individual.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some of these are also installed such that there are internal doors to each sleeping area.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB currently has about 1,100 rental flats with partitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: About half of these are vacant and available to JSS households.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While most of the flats were fitted with partitions while vacant, about 50 flats had partitions installed in-situ, at the request of tenants who are already living there.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This in-situ installation was a new offer we rolled out last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Interested tenants can contact their local HDB branch to request for partitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Apart from physical enhancements, we have also enhanced the support for tenants to become homeowners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last year, I announced that HDB will waive any subsequent rent increase for tenants who have made a downpayment for a new flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The median amount of rent saved by these families is about $150 per month, which they can put towards their upcoming new home, or other needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On Mr Gan Thiam Poh's suggestion to treat the rent paid as instalments for a future flat purchase, we have not done so as it is similar to giving the tenant a housing grant, which we already do through various schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Grants are also more equitable as the amount of subsidy would not vary with the tenants' length of stay in rental housing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our rental rates are tiered progressively based on income, to ensure that subsidies are allocated fairly, and targeted at those who need them most.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To mitigate the cliff effect at each tier, on a case-by-case basis, HDB waives the rent increase at tenancy renewal if it is a significant part of the household's increase in income.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond providing financial help, we have also intensified our efforts in other ways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We formed the Home ownership Support Team (HST) last year, to work closely with families towards home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The team is advising nearly 280 families and will guide them through when they are ready for home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the last three years, about 3,200 rental households have moved into their own homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Another 2,000 have booked a flat and are awaiting the completion of their new homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As the Malay saying goes, "sikit-sikit, lama-lama jadi bukit." This means "bit by bit, and over time, a little becomes a lot".

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Chairman, as we tackle the on-going COVID-19 outbreak and its economic fallout, we are reminded once again of how small and vulnerable Singapore is and how exposed we are to external forces beyond our control.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I am confident that Singaporeans will rise to the occasion.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are a resilient people, we have always faced tough odds, and we have confronted many difficult challenges before, in our nation's short history.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And each time, the Government and the citizens rally together; we deal with the issues head-on; and we emerge stronger and surer of what we can achieve together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Sixty years ago, this was one of the most pressing issues on the Government’s agenda.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Singaporeans lived in overcrowded slums, and the living conditions were appalling.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They said it was not possible to build so many flats in such a short period of time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It quickly ramped up the building of flats and addressed the acute housing shortage.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: My family is a beneficiary – my grandfather was a fisherman who lived in a kampong in Tanjong Rhu in the 1950s, and later when his children grew up and married, many were able to move out and purchase their own HDB flats, like my parents who got their flat in Marine Parade in the 1970s.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, many in my generation have benefited and now, I see the next generation, my nieces and nephews, getting married and purchasing their own HDB flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One just managed to get a flat in Bidadari and he is very happy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singaporeans all over the island will be able to share similar stories.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through home ownership, we have a tangible stake in our country and a share in our nation's progress.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through public housing, we all grow up together, regardless of backgrounds, and we forge a stronger sense of community and common identity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Enabling home ownership through HDB has been one of our most successful social policies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many have called it one of the most successful public housing programmes enacted anywhere in the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For this we have to thank generations of MND and HDB officers, past and present, who have worked hard to make all this happen.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we have much to be grateful for when we look back at what we have achieved together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we must never be complacent, and that is why we are always looking for ways to make HDB living even better.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, it is our evergreen mission to keep public housing affordable and accessible, so that every Singaporean household can have a home to call their own.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we continue to sell HDB flats at heavily subsidised prices and provide generous housing grants on top of that.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, HDB flat prices remain at less than five times of median household income.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You cannot find such affordable housing in any other major city in the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The ratio, the house price to income ratio, is nearly 10 times in London, Los Angeles and Sydney.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In Hong Kong, it is more than 20 times.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our affordability benchmark goes beyond the median income.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take the example of a first-timer couple with monthly income of $5,000, which is near the 30th percentile of resident household income.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They can buy a 4-room flat in a non-mature estate at a subsidised price of $330,000 and they will receive $45,000 in grants.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, inclusive of grants, the flat will cost less than five times their annual income.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The grants can be used to pay the down-payment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, they take a 25-year housing loan and their monthly mortgage is paid largely with their CPF savings, with little or zero cash outlay.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is our basic commitment to every generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a housing commitment not just to the higher or middle income groups but we will also ensure that lower income Singaporeans benefit.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Like the example I gave just now, even first-timers at the 30th percentile of household income, can purchase a new 4-room flat in a non-mature estate and service their housing loan with zero or very little cash outlay.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, for the vast majority of first-timers, the Singapore dream of being able to own your own home remains secure.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will make sure of that both now and in the future.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, we also want to have more affordable flats in the mature estates and a wider range of flat options to choose from, and Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Chong Kee Hiong both spoke about this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is more challenging to do so in mature estates, due to the limited space for new flats in these estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In some prime locations, the prices of resale HDB flats are beyond the reach of many young couples just starting out in life.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if this trend continues, it will mean that certain public housing estates can potentially become exclusive areas that only a few can afford and then this will lead to greater social stratification.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we do have to do something about this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to review it and we will share more details in the coming year when we are ready.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides affordability, we will also help Singaporeans to access their flats more quickly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members like Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Mohamed Irshad spoke about this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continually review and improve our sales processes to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For new BTO flats, we give priority for those looking for their first home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since last year, we have started sharing information on upcoming BTO sites six months in advance instead of just three months.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will try to do more, as suggested by Mr Gan Thiam Poh, but I am afraid it is not so easy to project forward for more than six months.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will be challenging to share this information too far in advance because there may well be unexpected changes along the way.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some households may need a flat more urgently.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we also offer balance flats for sale, many of which are completed or near completion.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, we have the Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) and, if there are still unselected flats after the SBF, we pool all of them together and we release them through what we call the Re-Offer of Balance Flats (ROF) exercises.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The initial take-up of the ROF flats has been positive.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we have received feedback and requests for the ROF to be done more frequently instead of just twice a year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, last year, we tried putting out some of these unselected flats on an open booking system for people to apply all year round.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, you can go for BTO flats – new flats which will be released four times a year, you can apply for a balance flat which will be put out twice a year, or you can go for open booking and apply online at almost any time of the year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, that is our first priority to ensure affordability and accessibility of flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second, we also support the diverse housing needs of different segments of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For needy households without other housing options or family support, we continue to provide them with public rental housing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the years, HDB has steadily increased the public rental supply.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For those who want specific locations, the waiting time may be longer, depending on availability of units in that particular area.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members, including Ms Anthea Ong, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Dr Lily Neo, asked for bigger rental units and dedicated units for single tenants, and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling has also explained our thinking on this matter.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We would, in fact, very much like to accommodate all of these requests.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The key constraint we have is one of land supply.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have to ensure that demand for both new rental and new sold flats in Singapore can be met on a sustainable basis, not just today, but over the coming decade and beyond.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is actually getting harder and harder to do as our island gets more built up.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we do need to take a pragmatic approach.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For single tenants, as Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun has said just now, most are prepared to share and are able to live in a rental flat together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For the few with medical conditions, we are prepared to consider their requests on an exceptional basis and allow them to stay in a rental flat by themselves.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For families, especially with children, the majority already live in our 2-room rental flats and, for very large families, we do our best to accommodate them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, for multi-nuclear families, we can offer them two rental units in the same block.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On a case-by-case basis, we will be prepared to offer larger families a 3-room rental flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ms Anthea Ong made the point about occupancy caps and I should clarify that these are caps imposed on HDB owners renting out their flats and the tenants who are renting these flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The occupancy caps do not apply to family members living together, be it in their own flat or a public rental flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the same time, we will continue to support public rental tenants towards home ownership.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members also spoke about this, including Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Arasu Duraisamy and Dr Lily Neo.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have announced several measures on this last year and the Senior Parliamentary Secretary has shared the progress on these initiatives.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For divorcees, we understand and recognise that their housing transitions can be stressful.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, Mr Louis Ng spoke about divorcees who are awarded shared care and control of a single child but are unable to agree on who can list the child in their flat application.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We understand that such agreement is not always possible, especially if the divorce was acrimonious.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members also spoke about this, including Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Arasu Duraisamy and Mr Mohamed Irshad.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do want to ensure that their children have a stable home to grow up in.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will assist all unwed parents who approach HDB with their housing needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For such cases, HDB will assess their situation holistically because their circumstances vary.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some Members did raise the point that such a case-by-case approach may cause more uncertainty amongst the applicants because they do not know whether their applications will be successful.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, let me clarify the approach that HDB takes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Next, for those who have insufficient finances and need a place to stay, then we will continue to consider them for public rental if this is in their child's best interests, taking into account inputs from social workers, if necessary.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Yet another group that we support is our seniors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many of them have their own homes but they are concerned about retirement savings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will try to help them unlock the value of their flat if they need to in several ways.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They can rent out their flat or spare bedrooms, they can right-size to a smaller flat, or they can sell a part of their lease to HDB under the Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through these engagements, we also receive feedback and ideas on how our schemes can be improved.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One feedback is that the schemes can be quite complex and we can simplify them further.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Regardless of the type of flat they sell, seniors can apply for the SHB as long as they buy a 3-room or smaller flat and get some proceeds from the move.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, effectively, someone staying in a 3-room flat in a mature estate who wishes to move to a 3-room flat in a non-mature estate, and can get some proceeds from that move, will still be eligible for an SHB.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A lateral move but because they are moving from a mature estate to a non-mature estate, they can unlock some proceeds and they will still be eligible for SHB.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Next, to receive the SHB, seniors must top up some proceeds from their move into their CPF Retirement Account.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is to ensure that they have adequate savings for retirement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, seniors will receive $1 in cash bonus for every $2 topped up to their CPF Retirement Account.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, if you have sales proceeds, you top up $60,000, you will get $30,000 in Silver Housing Bonus.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In line with this increase, we will also increase the maximum Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) bonus across all flat types.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means that owners of 3-room or smaller, 4-room, and 5-room or larger flats will get a larger bonus.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The maximum cash bonus will be $30,000, $15,000 and $7,500 respectively.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are also looking at alternative housing options for seniors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, we shared that MND is working with MOH to pilot assisted living, which allows seniors to buy a flat along with care services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Arasu Duraisamy asked about the status of this project.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Both Ministries have held several focus group discussions on the assisted living models.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They were generally very well received by seniors, particularly singles and those whose children have moved out.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Seniors were especially attracted to the idea of community living.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have incorporated the feedback into our pilot.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, this new pilot that we will be rolling out will have large communal spaces on every floor, not just on the void deck, but on every floor, where residents can gather and interact.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The flats will be sized at 32 sqm, with senior-friendly features like larger bathrooms and a layout that can be easily configured for mobility needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will launch the pilot with about 160 units in Bukit Batok in May this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: More details will be shared in the coming weeks, including the sales conditions, indicative flat prices and the payment options.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also want to make public housing more inclusive, especially for persons with disabilities and mobility issues, something which Miss Cheryl Chan highlighted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have made progress in this area in creating barrier-free access for all our HDB estates, but certainly more can be done.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Miss Cheryl Chan said, technology may well open up new possibilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We thank her for her ideas and the Government will continue to study this issue.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One area when it comes to barrier-free access is having lift access on every floor.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members have asked about this – Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Ong Teng Koon, and Mr Png Eng Huat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Members are aware, there are still about 150 blocks that are not eligible for the Lift Upgrading Programme (LUP).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To set things in context, we have managed to provide direct lift access for flats in the vast majority of HDB blocks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have done so by using innovative technical solutions and by exercising flexibility for some blocks even when they exceed the cost cap of $30,000 per household.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But for the remaining 150 blocks, for some of them, LUP is just not technically feasible, regardless of the cost.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For many others, the costs are very high.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is not just about having some flexibility above the cost cap but we are talking about costs that can be more than $200,000 per household in some cases.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Mr Png Eng Huat said – enough to buy another HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will continue to explore new technical methods to bring down the LUP cost, but it will not be so easy to make progress on this front.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the meantime, we know that some residents may urgently need direct lift access due to medical or mobility issues.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And really, it is more cost-effective to help them move to another flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, if anyone is in need and they need direct lift access, they do not want to wait, and the grant is available for them to move to a new place which will have direct lift access.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A third priority for us is to continue to rejuvenate our HDB towns and keep them vibrant for generations to come, and we have many upgrading programmes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Town Councils are generally responsible for regular and cyclical maintenance of common property, including building façades, and the Government supports the Town Councils for such work, so that the costs are not just borne by the Town Councils from their collections of service and conservancy charges (S&CCs).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, MND has provided additional grants to help Town Councils with their operating needs and long-term capital expenditure requirements, including for lift maintenance and lift replacement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the specific case that Mr Pritam Singh asked about, we will get back to him quite soon, based on the PE's assessment of what the damages were due to.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond the work of the Town Councils, there is Government upgrading through the Home Improvement Programme (HIP).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have finished selecting all flats built up to 1986 for Home Improvement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are starting with a bigger number to also help support the construction industry during this period.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Town Councils have submitted their nominations for this next phase of HIP, and we will inform the Town Councils of the selected projects later this week and then work can get started as soon as we can.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At around that time, our oldest HDB blocks will be about 60 years old and, if our Budget permits then, as we have said, we will initiate the second round of HIP, or HIPII, for these older flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will, almost every year be continuing with upgrading works.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides block-level programmes, at the precinct-level, we will refresh older precincts with new amenities through the on-going Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) and we will be selecting 20 NRP projects for implementation this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the past, we used to do about 14.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, we have raised it to 20 projects, partly to support the construction sector.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If there are new in-fill developments within an old precinct, then HDB, as the developer, will also provide for facilities to link up the old and new precincts, which is something that Mr Png has asked for.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I should say that HDB blocks are designed by a range of architects, not all by HDB.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The architects take great pride in their work.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will let them know how Mr Png feels about their void decks which are maze-like and confusing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I am sure they will want to take in feedback and continue to work on these designs to do better.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have selected nine towns and estates for ROH so far.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The remaking works that can be explored include refreshing of the town and neighbourhood centres, and enhancing of greenery and community spaces in parks or even areas under viaducts.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we will do all of this refreshing and rejuvenating while strengthening the distinctive heritage and identity of our individual housing estates, something which Mr Teo Ser Luck and many others have highlighted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will want to preserve and even strengthen their distinctive heritage and identity, even as we put in new features and rejuvenate these towns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also engage and work with residents closely in this endeavour so that we can remake our heartlands together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HIP, NRP and ROH are our key upgrading programmes which we will continue to press forward with.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At some point, as our flats and estates get older, we will need to more systematically redevelop and renew these older estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we have said that we will be introducing a new programme called the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We expect to roll out the first VERS project sometime after 2030.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a major programme and we will need to work through the details.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will take some time to do so and we will share that with Singaporeans when we are ready.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the meantime, we will make our towns greener and more sustainable.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members have asked about our plans for this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Tengah, our newest and greenest HDB town, offers a glimpse of what we can do and aim to do.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Tengah will be equipped with the latest sustainable features, including a centralised cooling system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will have dedicated walking and cycling paths and lots of community green spaces.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, as we push the boundaries in our new towns, we will do likewise in our older towns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we will be launching the new HDB Green Towns programme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is a 10-year plan to make existing HDB towns more environmentally sustainable and more liveable.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Using sensors, the system dims to provide just enough ambient lighting when common areas are unoccupied, then brightens again before residents enter an area.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is motion sensors but they are enhanced motion sensors, much better than what you have seen so far.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It uses up to 60% less energy than normal LED lighting.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also harness more renewable energy to power common services in HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are already installing solar panels on the rooftops of close to 50% of HDB blocks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: You do not seen that very often because very few people see HDB blocks from the sky.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But half of our HDB blocks today will have HDB panels on their rooftops.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, this will provide clean energy for our common services in our HDB estates and, in turn, benefit our residents.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second, we will recycle rain water and mitigate flood risks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To do that, we will pilot a new underground water detention system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Rainwater collected can be used for non-potable purposes, like washing of the void decks and watering of plants.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our preliminary studies suggest that such "cool paint" may be able to reduce ambient temperatures in HDB estates by up to two degrees.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will test this across several neighbourhoods to confirm its effectiveness before rolling it out across all estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This increases green cover and provides more green spaces for all the residents to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a major effort and the Government, Town Councils and our residents will all need to do our part.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Only then can we build greener and more sustainable HDB towns for our next generation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our efforts to green Singapore do not stop with our HDB towns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also push ahead with our efforts to build our future city.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One of Singapore’s defining features is our lush greenery and we will be doubling down on our greening strategy, as Second Minister Desmond Lee has elaborated just now.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our green strategy also covers our urban infrastructure and buildings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have made good progress in greening our buildings and we will continue to accelerate this effort, as Minister of State Zaqy explained.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have set bold targets to move towards cleaner vehicles, including electric vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On our part, MND will expand the necessary charging infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
