text: We will work with private companies to introduce more charging points at selected public carparks, taking into account the geographical spread of EV chargers, carpark usage, space availability for electrical upgrades and estate upgrading plans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Ong asked for some details on this but we are still working through the detailed plans and we will share more in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also continue with our longer term plans to rebuild and remake our city for the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have plans in the East, in the West and in the North-East around Changi Airport; in the West around Jurong Innovation District and Jurong Lake District; and in the North with the Punggol Digital District as well as Sungei Kadut.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the longer term, beyond the next 10 to 15 years, we have major sites for redevelopment, as Members would be aware, including the Paya Lebar Airbase when the military airbase moves out and the Greater Southern Waterfront.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are ambitious, major long-term plans which will take several decades to realise.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is an opportunity for all of us to start imagining what a future Singapore can be and to work towards realising it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Of course, we all recognise that the best-laid plans of Man do not always come to pass.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There will be unexpected challenges along the way.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the start of this year, no one could have predicted that we would be dealing with a virus outbreak today and that this virus outbreak would be potentially escalating into a global problem.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It reminds me of what our founding Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew, used to say.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: He said this twice, on two occasions during his birthday dinners.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: He said, and I quote: "Only a people who are willing to face up to their problems and be prepared to work with their leaders to overcome unexpected hardships with courage and resolution deserve to thrive and prosper." And that is why the theme of the Budget this year is "Unity".

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With a united purpose, we can overcome our current challenges.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We can continue to plan for tomorrow and we can continue to work together to build a better city and home.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I am glad to hear from the Minister that, this round, there will be many more homes selected for HIP and, certainly, the older part of Nee Soon South built in 1987 should be among the first batch.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I have five supplementary questions for Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad and one question for Minister Grace Fu.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The first question: just now Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad mentioned that there should be no discrimination against foreign contractors.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, why do we pay $6 million to a foreign contractor which is registered in Virgin Islands and BCA, being the agency championing —

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Second question, I mentioned about the contractor saying that the carpenters and tilers are no longer coming to Singapore.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Can BCA look into this so that they can continue to have workers?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And the third question is that, it is good that BCA has asked developers to help contractors, but then developers they have tight practical completion period and ABSD to comply with.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And the last question, I would like to ask how many Polytechnic graduates currently join the construction sector.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Because if I understood Minister of State correctly, he mentioned that they will be groomed to replace as S Pass holders.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: But as far as we understood, many of them, immediately upon graduation, they go overseas or head to a local University to get a degree instead of entering the workforce.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: My question to Minister Grace Fu is that, it seems that there is a very efficient, high rate of solving the problems reported to MSO.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The feedback that I got from residents is that MSO is very keen to close the case very fast.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Straightaway, they replied me, "Thank you for your report to MSO.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: We will revert to the relevant work unit".

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I asked them a question, "Can you take a photograph when the work is done so that I know that it is closed." And then, no further reply.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, I think many of my residents have similar experience.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: That is why the feedback to me that MSO is very keen to close the case though the end result is not what we want.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I am honoured to get five questions from Er Dr Lee Bee Wah.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It has to be on merit, based on the quality matrices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Unfortunately, specific to the tender, I cannot comment on LTA's evaluation because I do not have access to that particular tender.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But rest assured, our approach has been about building our local firms' capabilities and giving them that chance.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I have said, you have seen more and more local firms accessing larger projects either on their own or through joint ventures.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is where you also pick up new capabilities, new skills and new technologies that you can use and apply to meet the kind of requirements that we have.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For some of these projects, such as LTA tenders, I do understand.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some of these involving trains do have specific requirements.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there could be certain technical requirements that were evaluated.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, these are areas in which you have seen more and more local firms coming through; and certainly, we are giving more opportunities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This enables local firms to build their track record.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And you can also see that more are also being awarded larger public sector contracts over $85 million too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, to some extent, we have seen progress.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And I think it is good to see more local firms, as I have mentioned in my examples earlier, being able to take on these opportunities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On carpenters and tilers, we looked into this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is not easy to get foreign workers sometimes, especially with some skill-sets because it is not just about our environment here but also the environment there.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Contractors tell me too, that in the past they could get ready access to Chinese workers; but as China develops, they are paying their workers more over there, and there is less impetus for them to come here.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: When more and more countries develop, there will be opportunities out there.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our carpenters and tilers are typically from Malaysia, and you will probably find younger Malaysians being more educated too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, supply may come down.To some extent, it is more than just our local environment that causes some of these dynamics.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Member asked earlier on about the Project Completion period.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I have mentioned, we will monitor this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So far, there are just a few appeals.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Let us talk to the industry again and see how we can manage this better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And certainly for now, it is on case-by-case basis but we will continue to monitor the situation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On pro-rating the ABSD, or the extension of remission timelines today, I think we can still discuss and negotiate.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To some extent, we do not have to shift the whole mechanism or the whole system.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I think right now, the approach that we are taking is really on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Let us monitor and see how best we can help developers and builders cope with the current COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is not in our interest to make life difficult for our developers and builders.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is a growing sector and we do have long-term pipelines of projects that are being rolled out, not just in the public sector but also in the private sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We want our local companies to be able to address them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will help them as much as we can.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On Polytechnic graduates, I do not have the numbers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Perhaps the Member would like to file a Parliamentary Question because what she is asking for is specific in terms of pipeline and graduates.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, maybe file a Parliamentary Question in due course.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to address Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's question.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We look at the time taken and we pay particular attention to cases that take longer than usual.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Having said that, we do not stipulate the service standards for each of the agencies because the nature of cases can be different.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If there is litter that is not cleaned, someone can clean it up quite quickly.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But if there is a request for public lighting to be installed, then obviously, the cases would take longer.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We do recognise that even though service standards are not prescribed, public officers, knowing that MSO is watching, tend to want to do the right thing and try to close the cases as quickly as possible.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In many of these cases, it is about giving a better reply.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In cases where it is expected to take longer, such as doing maintenance in time, when we are doing a cyclical maintenance in three months' time or six months' time, we do want to go back and give the appropriate answer to the resident.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If we give the appropriate reply, I think we can manage the expectations of the residents better.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If you have received a reply from agencies but you are not satisfied with the reply, or if you do not think that your case or feedback has been satisfactorily addressed, you can indicate it through the poll rating and you can also follow up with subsequent submission on the same issue.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are paying attention to how we are closing the cases and we want to see that not only do we do it efficiently, we are also doing it effectively and from the residents' point of view, we are addressing their concern appropriately.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: Chairman, I would like to thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for her answer.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: In terms of the regulation of the pet animal trade, I feel that the past few years have focused a lot on the cats and the dogs, but the pet bird trade has largely been forgotten.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: The same pet bird shop looks exactly the same as 30 years ago.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: In terms of traceability, I think for pet birds, currently, there is possibly no traceability which is why someone is confident that they can distribute 800 birds by illegally smuggling them in.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: I hope that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary can step up enforcement of the pet bird as well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I am not quite sure if that was a question or a point.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And I would just like to share that if you look at the number of illegal bird smuggling cases, it has been coming down over the years.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I just like to give him the assurance that we have not forgotten about birds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am very happy that the person that is sitting on the chair I used to sit on also now asks animal-related questions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But if I could bring the topic back to cats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can I just ask Senior Parliamentary Secretary that the current rule is that you are not allowed to keep a cat in a HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, how and when does HDB enforce this ruling, because a lot of the residents I see, most of the time is because they complained against a neighbour and the neighbour, then realises, "Oh.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Now, I complain about the cat." And the cat becomes a sort of collateral and then, they are forced to remove the cat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The second clarification is back to the divorcees with shared care and control.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am very thankful that we will exercise flexibility for those where one party has already has private housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But could I ask further whether we can waive the mutual consent if both parties that have shared care and control are low income, meaning that both cannot really afford to buy from the open market and would need subsidised HDB flats?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The HDB will investigate if the feedback is related to pet-related disamenities, and it is not that a cat is a collateral in bad relations between neighbours.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB will investigate that the feedback is related to pet-related disamenities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And if really there is irresponsible cat ownership and this is found to be the reason, then HDB would advise the owner accordingly with the assistance of relevant agencies where necessary.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if they both need subsidised housing, on a case-by-case basis, if they are indeed lower income, they cannot afford to buy a home themselves, we will look at these cases and we will see what we can do to extend flexibility to them.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: I wish to thank the Minister, on behalf of the residents of Blocks 115 and 119 of Marsiling Rise for his kind and compassionate consideration of the situation with the introduction of the Lift Access Grant.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: I wish to ask the Minister whether such grant will be available to flat owners who have purchased the flat prior to the announcement today or will be available to subsequent owners as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: And if the granting of the Lift Access Grant will automatically enable them to buy a flat from the HDB or would they have to buy from the resale market?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: Can they sell the flat to the HDB or must they sell to the resale market; in which case, will future owners also be eligible for this grant?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If the person wants a flat very urgently, then getting it from the resale market makes a lot of sense.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If they want a new BTO flat nearby and if there are balance flats, HDB could consider allocating one, if there is a balance flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But that depends on whether there is availability of such a balance flat nearby.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the sale of their present flat, we will require them to sell the flat before making the new transaction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will try our best to help them but, in the first instance, it is the responsibility of the homeowner to engage an agent and look at whether or not they can sell the flat in order to make the purchase, whether it is new or resale.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If they do face difficulties, then I will ask them to approach the HDB branch and we will see whether we can find ways to help them.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: Earlier in my speech, I asked whether there are assessments by HDB for applicants of Joint Singles Scheme (JSS) to ensure that they are free from mental illnesses and medical conditions before compelling them to stay together.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: Because I also noticed that HDB always gives applicants a list of names for them to call themselves to choose their own tenants to share with.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: So, as Minister Wong earlier said, we have been improving our HDB policies to facilitate Singaporeans in their housing needs.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: JSS has been around for the last 30 years.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: So, why can we not tweak this to facilitate just the most vulnerable group in our society?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Dr Neo for the suggestion.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, it has been tweaked, it has been evolving.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do provide flexibility for those with medical conditions and with exceptional circumstances to stay on their own.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The reason why we cannot depart from this and say, "Everyone live on their own now", is the real constraint which I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If we are going to double, triple the number of rental units that we have in order to accommodate them, because every JSS tenant wants to split up, we do not have land.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, there is no land available to build more.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have got to build new flats, we have got to build new rental flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are not trying to be hard-hearted about this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is just not enough space to build so many more new housing units.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We try to optimise where we can and as the Senior Parliamentary Secretary said just now, when we did a survey of JSS tenants, the majority of them do get along and are okay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are dealing with a minority and we can manage that if they do not get along, if there are medical conditions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If they do not get along in the first instance, let us try to find ways to pair you up with somebody else.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you have medical conditions, then we will look at your case, and we will consider allowing you to stay on your own, if there is a need to.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, I will allow your question if it is not about cats.

speaker: The Chairman
text: You have already asked a question about cats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I just want to confirm with the Senior Parliamentary Secretary that when HDB receives a complaint, they go down and investigate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If the cat is not causing any disamenities, the resident will not be asked to remove the cat.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, your last question.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Just now the Minister of State mentioned that due to the change in their own country, that is why the carpenters and the tilers are not coming.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: That could be part of the reason but what we heard from the industry is that they are not coming to Singapore but they go to some other countries.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: That is why I urge BCA to study and see what is the reason they do not come to Singapore, so that we do not suffer if we do not tackle this problem now.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The next question is about cutting of the S Pass.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: We need the S Pass holders for DfMA, for PPVC, more so because they are more skillful.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: If the Polytechnic graduates do not join the industry, by cutting the S Pass, really, will give our construction industry a double-whammy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I hope you will really look into this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I was just saying, some examples provided were that the supply is also changing, as well as demographics.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But of course, if they go to other countries, then, basically, it could also mean that we do not pay well enough and other countries are also paying better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There are different reasons, but I do agree – let us not come to conclusions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Let us do our study, which I said we will do.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Apart from the IHLs, we are also putting on stream PCPs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As we have shared in many of our speeches earlier, even MOM in the Budget, that the Government is putting a bit of focus into mature workers to see how we can transform and move along.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I have also shared, in terms of those coming from the manufacturing sector, for example, they can move to DfMA.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There are different skills required beyond just the Polytechnic graduates; mid-careers can also shift into such sectors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We do see some slowdown in certain sectors such as process and marine, but these are areas in which we can also look to see how some of the workers can be moved into construction as we build.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What I hope is that we continue to attract our Polytechnic and ITE graduates.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Yes, some of the Polytechnic graduates may move on to University and ITE graduates move to Diploma too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We need to continually build that pathway for them, so that a career in construction also becomes more attractive.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are looking at all levels, not just on the IDD, BIM or DfMA side.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are some of the efforts that we are putting in place, whether it is PCP, BIM, attracting mid-careers, as well as those coming in from the University, Polytechnics and ITEs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The grunt work of construction is still being provided for, so that we continue to grow and build our infrastructure.
